bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Delayed/patchy summer season impacting fans/coolers; War-geopolitical input cost inflation; Market share loss in Fans due to BLDC technology gap; Demand uncertainty limiting price pass-through.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Cautiously optimistic; Transparent about Consumer Products struggles; Confident in Lighting trajectory; Emphasis on 'cultural change' and sustainable profitability over volume push.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Management explicitly stated they will reinvest Lighting margin gains to accelerate growth rather than bottom-line expansion; Fan segment weakness specifically tied to lack of competitive BLDC offerings vs. traditional induction strength; Inventory correction in coolers still ongoing but deemed non-material for full year.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Legacy spanning over eight decades as a household FMEG name and vital pillar of the Bajaj Group
- Pan-India distribution scale: 850+ distributors (Board's overview) / 2,000+ channel partners (MD&CEO message), nearly 2,00,000+ retail outlets, and 770+/778 consumer care centres reaching 19,000 pin codes
- Multi-brand 'house of brands' portfolio (Bajaj, Morphy Richards, Nirlep) each anchored in a distinct value proposition, spanning the full price spectrum
- Full brand ownership of Morphy Richards (post-acquisition) enabling sharper premiumisation and margin control versus the prior licensing arrangement
- Engineering depth in professional lighting projects (smart cities, stadiums, industrial complexes, tunnels) described by the MD & CEO as a real competitive moat
- Digital enablement across the trade network (DMS, Sarathi App, DSO App, Power BI) strengthening distributor governance and transparency
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Geopolitical and macroeconomic uncertainty (Middle East conflict, shifting trade policies) — The AR flags high macroeconomic uncertainty, shifting trade policies and continuing fiscal challenges; geopolitical tensions in the Middle East add pressure, with disruptions in key shipping routes potentially raising freight costs and lead times, and volatility in crude oil and base metal prices (copper, aluminium) potentially raising input costs — directly relevant given Bajaj Electricals' exposure to copper/aluminium as commodity inputs.
- Rupee depreciation / currency risk — The rupee hit an all-time low of approximately ₹95/USD during the year, driven by Middle East conflict volatility and FPI outflows; a weakening rupee accelerates domestic inflation by raising import costs (especially crude oil) and widens the trade deficit, which the Company is exposed to given import dependence in its supply chain.
- Tariff-related trade disruption — Tariff-related trade disruptions and volatility in capital flows may intermittently affect exports and investor sentiment, per the MD&A macro outlook.
- Supply-chain disruption from the West Asia conflict — Supply-chain disruptions due to the West Asia conflict could tighten the availability of key inputs for downstream sectors, including plastics and aluminium — materials relevant to the Company's manufacturing base.
- Import dependence and tightening regulatory/quality enforcement — Import dependence exposes companies (including Bajaj Electricals) to currency fluctuations and supply disruptions from geopolitical conflicts, which may elevate input costs; separately, regulatory bodies such as the Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) are strictly enforcing Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) norms, leading to increased product recalls and legal notices for non-compliant goods on e-commerce platforms.
- Intense competition and margin pressure — Competition remains vigorous, intensified by established global and domestic players and low barriers to entry; aggressive pricing, frequent discounts and new product launches can weigh on margins over time.
- Operating deleverage / profitability compression — The Consolidated Financial Analysis shows revenue, EBITDA, EBIT and PAT margins all declining year-on-year in FY26, with the Company moving from profit to loss at the PBT/PAT/Return-on-Net-Worth level — reflecting an operating-deleverage risk if demand softness persists.
- Internal control gaps in automated systems — The external Internal Auditor identified certain non-significant automated controls not configured during the year; these were mitigated by compensating manual controls, but represent a residual internal-control risk to monitor.

business.body: Bajaj Electricals Limited is a fast-moving electrical goods (FMEG) company with a legacy spanning over eight decades, operating across Consumer Products (fans, home and kitchen appliances, cooking solutions and grooming products) and Lighting Solutions (addressing both consumer and professional applications). With the addition of switchgears and wires under the Bajaj Secura brand, and strategic expansion into solar solutions, the Company has broadened its footprint within the electrical ecosystem. It sells through a multi-brand, 'house of brands' portfolio (Bajaj, Morphy Richards, Nirlep) to millions of consumers pan-India.

- **Lighting Solutions:** Consumer lighting, Professional lighting (smart cities, stadiums, industrial complexes, tunnels)
- **Switchgears and Wires:** Bajaj Secura (brand)
- **Solar Solutions:** Solar (strategic foray, adjacent to distribution network)

outlook.body:
- Accelerating domestic sourcing, localising critical components, and reducing single-country dependencies in response to tariff and geopolitical supply-chain risk.
- Operating a clear two-brand strategy: the BAJAJ brand (refreshed identity) serves mass and aspirational segments, while the fully-owned Morphy Richards addresses the upper mid-market and premium lifestyle segment.
- Accelerating premiumisation — launching upgraded, energy-efficient and higher-value SKUs (400+ new SKUs across consumer products and lighting in recent years) and moving the product mix upward while defending category-leading positions (No.1 in mixer-grinders, No.2 in water heaters).
- Deepening distribution quality over mere distribution width, alongside continued expansion of channel reach into underserved and rural markets.
- Deliberate inventory correction in the Consumer Products business carried out through H1 and Q3 FY26 with channel partners, to establish a cleaner, healthier inventory base for more disciplined, sustainable growth from Q4 FY26 onwards.
- Driving execution rigour and cost/working-capital efficiency across the business (supply chain, sales, service) through lean initiatives and digital tools to improve inventory turns and optimise cost structure.
- Investing in future-ready capabilities: strengthening the digital backbone, data analytics for demand forecasting, and accelerating e-commerce/omnichannel presence.
- Foray into Solar, Switchgear and Wires categories, adjacent to the existing distribution network and aligned with the government's housing and electrification agenda.
- Partnership with TIH Foundation for smart lighting solutions for smart cities, reflecting an ambition to move from selling products to solving for integrated environments.
- Sustainability positioned as embedded operating practice (not an add-on), with continued BRSR-framework disclosure and greater granularity on environmental performance.
- Dividend for the year is recommended by the Board and, per the AGM notice resolution, is paid out of the Company's free reserves; the Board's practice (evidenced elsewhere in this AR bundle) has been to maintain the per-share dividend even in a loss-making year as a signal of continued commitment to shareholders. This bundle does not carry the narrative text of a separately articulated Dividend Distribution Policy beyond the AGM resolution language.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Company forayed into the switchgear segment with the launch of the BAJAJ SECURA brand (switchgear and wires), described as a strategic expansion of the lighting solutions business that extends the Company's generational expertise into a new category. The Company broadened its international footprint in FY2026 through targeted market initiatives: in Sri Lanka it introduced new appliance categories and strengthened the Morphy Richards presence through its established partner; in Nepal it implemented DMDC-based distribution for ceiling fans while consolidating appliance sales; in Dubai efforts focused on re-export partners with a consistent monthly push to grow market share in the ceiling fan segment. Looking to FY2027, the Professional Lighting business plans to strengthen its competitive edge through R&D and digital integration, with an emphasis on ultra-efficient solutions that reduce carbon footprints; growth efforts will be pursued across infrastructure, sports, office spaces and data centres, alongside diversification into solar solutions, and the Company will implement AI-driven Tender Intelligence Analytics to improve bid selection and win probability. Manufacturing operations are organised across four manufacturing sites at Nashik, Chakan, and Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (Maharashtra), supported by 18 warehouses; overall capacity utilisation across all plants stood at 59% for FY2026.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India's consumer durable sector is projected to grow at an 11% CAGR in FY2027, supported by rising consumption, broader rural reach and growing global investment interest.
- PLI Scheme allocation of ₹1,004 crore for FY2026-27 is expected to support capacity augmentation, local manufacturing and encourage new entrants in appliances.
- Fan industry demand is being driven by a shift to BLDC motors and premium/smart models, rising urbanisation, El Nino-led hot summers, rising disposable income and rural electrification (first-time purchases).
- Stricter BEE energy-efficiency and star-labelling norms are expected to elevate product standards and expedite replacement cycles, sustaining baseline demand.
- India's professional lighting market is projected to grow from USD 354.33 million (2025) to USD 645.62 million by 2031 at a 10.52% CAGR, driven by smart-cities/urban infrastructure spend and demand for energy-efficient solutions.
- Consumer lighting demand is supported by smart-home/IoT adoption and government programmes such as UJALA and PLI schemes anchoring supply-chain resilience.
- Company's own exposure to weather-sensitive categories (coolers, fans) was partially offset by robust demand in core non-seasonal segments such as kitchen appliances.
- India's continued infrastructure push, a rising aspirational middle class, and increasing penetration of branded electrical products in Tier II/III cities are cited as durable demand tailwinds.
- Tariff barriers, supply chain reconfiguration, and commodity cost volatility (copper, aluminium) are flagged as headwinds affecting input costs and margins.
- India GDP growth is projected at 6.9% for FY2026-27, with CPI inflation projected at 4.6%, supporting the broader consumption/investment backdrop for the business.
- Professional lighting projects business continues to serve smart cities, stadiums, industrial complexes, and tunnels, described as demonstrating both technical capability and margin discipline.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Bajaj Electricals delivered a modest Q4FY26 with Lighting Solutions hitting record margins (8.5% annual) while Consumer Products faced losses due to delayed summer and intentional channel de-stocking. The strategic pivot from volume-push to demand-led sell-through is progressing, with inventory normalization expected to drive a rebound in FY27, though fan market share erosion due to BLDC gaps remains a critical near-term headwind.
